lines.text: That little plastic button in a Thanksgiving turkey has no battery and no electronics. So how does it know the bird is done?
Inside is a spring loaded red stick, held down by a tiny blob of metal, similar to solder.
That alloy is designed to melt right around turkey done temperature.
When the meat around it gets hot enough, the metal turns to liquid, lets go of the stick, and the spring shoots it up. Pop.
The idea came from a turkey farmer who borrowed it from fire sprinklers, which use a melting metal plug to release water.
But they can pop early. So double check with a thermometer: 165 degrees Fahrenheit in the thickest parts.
